summary.description: For the currently set filter, this page shows the dataset and abuse statistics for each of the monitored accounts. This gives the same information as you would get by manually selecting each account in the filter, but in a much easier way.

graphs.overview: For each account we calculate two different abuse percentages. Firstly there is the percentage of abusive posts within all posts relevant to the account (but not by the account). Secondly there is the percentage of replies to the account which are abusive. The full details of the accounts are listed ordered by the first of these measures, while both are shown in the accompanying graphs.

twitter.description: For each Twitter account of interest we collect Tweets that are either by the account, a reply to the account, which @mention the account, or which include either the screen name or the user's name. We currently collect this data once a day, each time collecting the full previous day. This results in some overlap but ensures that we don't miss any data.

youtube.description: YouTube data collection differs from that of most other platforms in that usually the people we are interested in don't have their own channels. Instead we search using their name and collect all comments on the top 500 results. We do this once a day which does result in some overlap but ensures we continue to get the most relevant comments for each user.

mastodon.description: Data collection for Mastodon accounts starts by collecting every post the user has made (this are available in their publically accessiable outbox). For each of these posts we then recersively retrieve every public reply. This frequently involves accessing many different Mastodon servers not just that used by the user of interest. As yet we have not implemented a way of collecting just the new posts/replies and so currently we periodocally re-collect everything; it is envisaged that this will change in the short term to something more effiecient.

tiktok.description: The data we currently collect from TikTok contains very little extra information over and above the video description or comment text. Specifically we only get user information for videos not comments. Depending on what we have collected (i.e. have we simply taken all videos from a single channel or have we run a search query) there may be very little useful information displayed below.

settings.title: Settings

language.title: Display dashboard in:
language.description: The language used throughout the dashboard. Note this does not include translating the posts themselves.

maxCSVRows.title: Max CSV Rows
maxCSVRows.description: In a number of places within the dashboard you can download a CSV file of the matching posts. In some cases this may involve a very large amount of posts (and hence data). This option allows you to limit the download to a maximum number of posts. The default of 0 signifies that all matching posts should be downloaded.

anonymousMode.title: Anonymous Mode
anonymousMode.description: When taking screenshots for presentations etc. it is good practice to ensure that the posts (especially those labelled as being abusive) are anonymized. When enabled this option replaces all profile images with the default image, and converts the name and handle of the account into a version in which all but the first two characters are replaced by *. Note that posts by the focus of the dashboard are not affected.

complianceMode.title: Compliance Mode
complianceMode.description: Posts are often deleted after they are sent, either by the original author choosing to remove them or because the account is deleted or suspended. Deleted posts should not be kept, but it is impossible to gauge levels of online abuse without making use of deleted posts. This option is a half way point in that it blurs out the entire post's content, whilst making it clear a post did exist. This option is independent of the anonymous mode, although both should probably be enabled before screenshots are taken or public demos given.

settings.afterUpdate: Settings which take effect after an update

topicMode.title: Aggregate topics by
topicMode.description: By default we aggregate topics by what we refer to as their 'theme'. Themes are a set of categories, originally defined by the UK Government, which cover ideas such as the economy, defense, public health. Whilst this categorization is useful it is rather UK centric and doesn't always work well when the focus of the index is from outside the UK. In such cases you can use the 'subtheme' instead which is based more around the detected topic phrases rather than their category.

abusiveReplies.title: Minimum Abusive Replies
abusiveReplies.description: When considering individual accounts which have sent abusive replies, only show those which have sent more than this number.

abusiveRetweets.title: Minimum Abusive Retweets
abusiveRetweets.description: When considering individual accounts which have retweeted abusive replies, only show those which have retweeted more than this number.

abuse_triggers.paragraph_1: This table shows all posts by the monitored account(s) which received at least one abusive reply, ordered by the number of abusive replies they received. Details are the total number of replies, the number of abusive replies (both the raw number and as a percentage of the replies), and the time from the posts being created to the first abusive reply.
abuse_triggers.paragraph_2: Clicking on a post will open it within the conversation explorer to allow a more detailed view of the replies. If the post isn't a link this means that whilst there are replies within our collection, we don't have the original post by the monitored account. In that case the time taken for the first abusive reply to appear will also be blank as we are unable to calculate it.
abuse_triggers.paragraph_3: This histogram shows how quickly posts by the monitored account(s) receive their first abusive reply. Each bar shows how many posts by the monitored account(s) received their first abusive reply within that minute window. For example, if the first bar has a value of 10 then this means that ten posts by the monitored account(s) received their first abusive reply within the first 60 seconds after being posted. The graph shows similar bars for the first hour after posts are posted by the monitored account(s).
